significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds: the rational solutions of L'Huilier's equation in the proper range are exactly the two-right-side family and the eight sporadic tuples of the source (one in Λ₁ and the seven of Λ₂), so by the source's Proposition 2.2 these are the only measurements of proper rational spherical triangles, and the seven with three distinct sides are the only such triangles. The proof is computer-assisted. In tangent coordinates the equation becomes a vanishing sum of 23 roots of unity. The new step is a line lemma: if the equation holds along a whole line of parameters through a proper point, the behaviour at the two ends of the segment forces the line into the two-right-side family. With the polygon inequality this gives a rank condition at every other solution, which shows that only the primes 2, 3, 5, 7 divide the common denominator and bounds their exponents, so the denominator divides 352,800 = 2⁵·3²·5²·7². An exact search over these denominators finishes the classification. Lean defines the solution set Ω₂ and the sets Λ₁, Λ₂ literally from the source and proves Ω₂ = Λ₁ ∪ Λ₂ with no hypotheses; the line lemma, the prime support, the exponent bounds and the whole finite search (replayed in the kernel in certified batches, with proofs that the batches cover every case) are inside Lean.
significance.caveat: One link is outside Lean: Wang's own Proposition 2.2 (Ω₁ = Ω₂, printed and proved in the source), which identifies the measurements of proper rational spherical triangles with the rational solutions of L'Huilier's equation; Lean proves the classification of those solutions. The result is Conjecture 1.6 in the numbering of arXiv v1 (the only arXiv version); it is not the source's other conjecture on the trigonometric equation (Conjecture 3.2, MathDB 361007), which remains open. The proof is computer-assisted: a finite exact search, replayed in the Lean kernel in 7,688 modules (about 1.38 million generated lines). Dvornicich, Lombardo, Veneziano and Zannier (arXiv:2404.02559) wrote that Wang's main conjecture should be amenable to their methods; the method here is of the kind they expected (vanishing sums of roots of unity and a finite search), and the new step is the line lemma. The journal versions (Int. J. Number Theory for the source, Math. Ann. for Dvornicich et al.) could not be read (reviewer's probabilities that they settle the conjecture: about 0.03 and below 0.02). Root's rebuild needed more memory than the standard runner allows: Lean's heap threshold was raised from 3,500 MB to 5,500 MB for the search modules and to 14,000 MB (with a 16 GiB guard) for the last six; this is a resource setting and does not affect what the kernel checks. All work is by AI and no human has checked it: the proof, the Lean code and the paper are by GPT-6.2 Sol lanes; the adversarial review before Lean (not routine 0.75) and the final check (0.75) are by two separate Claude Opus 5.5 lanes.
